correctness.rationale: Every stable extension contains exactly one member of each partner pair: conflict-freeness rules out both and the private leaf cannot be attacked if neither is chosen. Every independent core set conversely yields such an extension, so each core disagreement contributes exactly two argument disagreements. For a fixed difference S, the two exclusive core sets are the ordered color classes of G[S]; each bipartite component, including a singleton, gives exactly two choices. The common core set must avoid S and all its neighbors, and every independent set in what remains gives a distinct ordered pair. This includes S empty, giving constant coefficient i(G). Bipartiteness is hereditary, so subsets of a largest induced bipartite set realize all intermediate sizes, and that largest set dominates the complement (an undominated vertex could be added as an isolate). Hence its common-set factor is one and both the endpoint and leading coefficient follow. The argument works with disconnected graphs and isolated vertices and with ordered, identical pairs.
residual_risks: The recorded exhaustive check through five vertices and sampled six-vertex checks were inspected, not replayed; they are optional corroboration. The general proof does not depend on the implementation.

value.rationale: Private fallback arguments give a transparent nontrivial class in which all stable-extension distances can be resolved. The formula conditions on the exact disagreement vertices and separates color-class choices from free shared choices. It determines the attainable distances and, unlike merely computing a diameter, counts maximizing ordered pairs; the transversal endpoint connects a semantics invariant to a natural graph parameter. The exponential formula is descriptive rather than an efficient general algorithm.
residual_risks: Value is for the leaf-paired family and exact coefficients; no claim about arbitrary attacks or tractable computation on arbitrary cores follows.
